bullets.title: Record Nasdaq Short Position + NYSE Market Breadth Strength Diverge
bullets.body: Asset managers and hedge funds have built the largest Nasdaq futures short position in history, yet NYSE has not registered a single 80% downside volume day in 2026 — a phenomenon unseen in at least 30 years. Broad US index ETFs are back at all-time highs, but semiconductors and transports lag, flagging a potential leadership divergence worth watching.

bullets.title: Nvidia Ohio/OpenAI Mega-Deal: $105B Backstop, $1.5B SB Energy Investment, 4.25 GW
bullets.body: Nvidia secured land, power and shell capacity at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio (4.25 IT-GW) through a 20-year OpenAI lease, while reducing its financial guarantee from $250B to ~$120B and investing $1.5B directly into SB Energy. Goldman estimates $489B in AI-related capex YTD, already exceeding all of 2025's $322B; big tech has now disclosed $2.4–3T in off-balance-sheet AI commitments that debt/FCF-focused investors are beginning to scrutinize.

bullets.title: Anthropic Revenue 14x YoY to $11.5B in 2Q; Projects $190-200B by 2028
bullets.body: Anthropic posted Q2 revenue of $11.5B, up ~14-fold year-over-year, and achieved a second straight quarter of positive adjusted operating income. The company is projecting FY28 revenues of $190–200B, well ahead of OpenAI's ~$40B run-rate; 22V Research estimates Anthropic at a $100–120B annualized revenue exit in 2026 with compute shortage persisting through end-2027 at ~75% probability. These prints are being cited by the buyside as the key upside catalyst for semiconductors.

bullets.title: AI Capex Crowding Out Buybacks; S&P Concentration at Record Highs
bullets.body: The S&P 500 cash return to net income ratio fell below 60% (lowest since 2010) as AI capex displaces buybacks; top 10 S&P 500 names now represent ~39–42% of index market cap/earnings, up from ~20% in 2005. Margin debt YoY growth has been above 55% for over a year — a pace unseen since 1998 — while hedge fund net long/short leverage rebounded to 58% from 47%, near YTD highs.

bullets.title: Empire Manufacturing Surges to 20.6 — Strongest Since December 2021
bullets.body: The August Empire Manufacturing Index jumped 5 points to 20.6, highest since 2021; the ISM-adjusted reading came in at 55.4%, with capex plans and forward expectations both gaining. Prices paid rose while prices received fell, pushing the margin proxy to a cycle low, though Morgan Stanley's ISM model suggests industrial strength persisting through 1H 2027.

bullets.title: July US Retail Sales Down 0.6% MoM — Sharpest Drop Since May 2025
bullets.body: US July headline retail sales fell 0.6% month-over-month, the sharpest decline since May 2025, with nonstore retail down 2.2% post-Prime Day and consumer sentiment dropping ~8%. Clothing (+1.8%), health/personal care (+0.7%) and restaurants/bars (+0.6%) were the only categories positive; motor vehicles, gas stations and furniture all declined.

bullets.title: China Consumer Data Collapses: July Retail Sales +0.6% YoY, Miss vs +1.5% Consensus
bullets.body: China July retail sales slipped to +0.6% YoY (vs. +1.0% in June and +1.5% consensus), with offline sales declining 0.3% and apparel turning negative. Gold/jewelry fell 10% YoY despite gold prices up >20%, suggesting demand waiting for better entry. JP Morgan does not expect earnings cuts to have bottomed and sees consumer stocks reflecting caution rather than recovery.

bullets.title: Japan 10-Year JGB Yields Hit 30-Year High at 2.93%; BoJ Hike Expected by October
bullets.body: Japan's 10-year bond yield reached 2.93% (highest since 1996), with 2Q real GDP coming in at +1.1% q/q annualized vs. 2.0% consensus — the gap driven by a record +3.6% GDP deflator. Markets now expect the BoJ to hike to 1.25% no later than October, with the yen hovering near 160.

bullets.title: Dollar Weakening; BofA's Hartnett Says 'Anything But Dollar' — Gold Sees $6.3B Inflow
bullets.body: The US dollar is falling on receding rate-hike expectations, with gold showing a -0.93 inverse correlation to USD over the past three months. BofA's Hartnett recommends gold as the best hedge against dollar weakness, bond losses and asset inflation; gold funds attracted $6.3B last week, the largest inflow since January 2026.

bullets.title: 30-Year Treasury Yield at 5.30%; AI Bond Issuance Adding ~0.3ppts to 10Y Yield Rise
bullets.body: The 30-year Treasury yield is at 5.30%, with AI-driven corporate bond issuance contributing approximately 0.3 percentage points to the rise in 10-year yields. Duration risk is emerging from lease-term divergence between neo-cloud providers (shorter contracts at premium pricing) and hyperscalers (longer-term deals).

bullets.title: Iran Deal Odds Collapse to 13-16%; Hormuz Traffic Halts, Brent Near $90
bullets.body: The US-Iran 60-day ceasefire deadline expired Monday with no agreement; Strait of Hormuz traffic halted and prediction markets put deal probability at 13-16% through 2029. Brent crude bounced back near $90/bbl. 22V Research flags oil-yield correlation as unusually high, with Hormuz escalation capable of spiking oil above $100 and reigniting macro volatility.

bullets.title: Data Center Power Buildout Faces Community Pushback; Texas ERCOT Auditing 474 GW of Requests
bullets.body: Texas is auditing 474 GW of pending ERCOT interconnection requests (~90% data center-related) with a likely 1-3 month pause. Virginia's Rider T1 moves Dominion toward 'cost causer pays' for direct-connect transmission. Morgan Stanley views community opposition as a development constraint rather than a communications problem, turning bullish on off-grid/onsite power plays and colocation operators with established community track records.

bullets.title: GE Vernova Turbine Orders Hit Record in 2Q (+71% YoY); 2.5 GW Gas+SMR Plant Signed in Texas
bullets.body: Global turbine orders rose 71% year-over-year in Q2, the highest quarter on record, with Big-3 OEMs representing ~77% of orders. Blue Energy and GEV signed a 2.5 GW combined gas+SMR plant in Victoria, TX targeting a 2027 FID, with gas turbines delivering ~1 GW by 2030 and BWRX-300 SMRs adding ~1.5 GW from 2032.

bullets.title: Copper Hits All-Time High; Commodities Broadly Inflationary
bullets.body: Copper rallied 1.1% to all-time highs Monday morning amid a London supply squeeze. Broader commodity complex is inflationary with butter, barley, OJ, coffee all rising. Natural gas bucked the trend, down 3% and in a bearish trend per Hedgeye.

bullets.title: Q2 Earnings: Aggregate S&P EPS Growth Running +50.5% YoY as Season Winds Down
bullets.body: With Q2 earnings season nearly complete, aggregate year-over-year EPS growth stands at +50.5%. Russell 2000 results show aggregate earnings 2.0% above expectations and revenues 3.6% above expectations, with 136 of 2000 index stocks (82% of market cap) reported.

bullets.title: NAHB Housing Index +1 to 35 in August; Housing Stocks Up 16% from May Lows Flagged as Crowded
bullets.body: The NAHB Housing Market Index ticked up 1 point to 35 in August on current conditions alone, with sales expectations and buyer traffic flat. 22V notes housing stocks are up 16% from May lows despite 30-year yields near July highs; the ITB/TLT spread approaching a prior downtrend signals 18-22% correction risk within two months.

bullets.title: US-China Robotics Decoupling Begins; FCC Ban on Foreign Mobile Robots
bullets.body: Bernstein says the FCC ban on new foreign-made mobile robots marks the start of a US-China robotics decoupling, with spillover risk to AI chips, investments, and rare earths. China could retaliate through data controls or rare-earth magnets.

bullets.title: PE Secondary Market on Track for Record Annual Volume; 1H26 Hits $118B (+15% YoY)
bullets.body: Global PE secondary market volume reached $118B in 1H26, up 15% versus 1H25, putting 2026 on pace to exceed the 2025 record of $240B. GP-led transactions are now the majority (53%) for the first time since 2021, with single-asset continuation vehicles representing 68% of that volume. Average LP portfolio pricing stable at 87% of NAV.

bullets.title: UBS Equity Strategy: Buy AI Infrastructure and Electrification; NDX Over XRT
bullets.body: UBS favors AI infrastructure, European Electrification, and healthcare/GLP-1 themes at top of their framework; prefers NDX over XRT on 12-month forward EPS trends. Taiwan and South Korea rank highest among countries on semiconductor/tech hardware strength. UK Homebuilders, European Consumer Cyclicals, and AI-disrupted consumer stocks sit at the bottom of their rankings.

bullets.title: China 5Y Bond Yield Hits 20-Month Low; Property Investment -19.2% YoY in Jan-July
bullets.body: China's 5-year bond yield crashed 7% to a 20-month low Monday, signaling deflationary pressure and potential recession risk. Separately, China Jan-July property development investment declined 19.2% year-over-year. China's FX reserves posted the largest quarterly increase in 12+ years ($74.7B in Q2) as authorities absorbed strong foreign-currency inflows.
